text:
lauren: hey folks, day 1! ran the quickstart but hit a couple weird issues:

1) brew install openssl gives headers in /opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1 but node-gyp fails unless I export CPATH/LDFLAGS. whats the usual minimal fix?

miguel: welcome :wave: for mac M1 we add to ~/.zprofile:

  export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/lib"
  export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)/include"

then reinstall node modules that need native builds. also try `npm rebuild` after setting env.

lauren: thanks. 2) git-lfs kept asking for credential helper and failing on large files when cloning. do we enable system git-lfs or the repo has hooks?

dotfiles-admin: we vendor a small gitconfig in dotfiles that enables credential helper cache and lfs: add this to ~/.gitconfig if you want persistent creds:

  [credential]
    helper = osxkeychain
  [filter "lfs"]
    clean = git-lfs clean -- %f
    smudge = git-lfs smudge -- %f
    process = git-lfs filter-process --skip-smudge
    required = true

also run `git lfs install --system` once.

lauren: got it. 3) npm global installs still try to write to /usr/local on my machine. i thought brew/homebrew on m1 uses /opt/homebrew. any npmrc recommendation to avoid sudo?

miguel: create ~/.npmrc with `prefix=${HOME}/.npm-global` and add `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to your profile. avoid sudo. if using asdf node plugin we prefer using that as the primary node runtime so you don't mix brew node and asdf shims.

lauren: i'm using asdf for node per onboarding. when i switch shells i still sometimes see the brew node (older) earlier in PATH. ran `which -a node` and saw both. how to make sure asdf shims come first?

dotfiles-admin: ensure asdf init runs early in your login profile before you add /opt/homebrew/bin. e.g. in ~/.zprofile put:

  . $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
  export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH"

then open a fresh terminal and `asdf reshim`.

lauren: last tiny thing: onboarding script prompted me to add SSH key but i also need access to a private dataset in the s3 bucket. who owns that?

infra-bot: Welcome @lauren! For dataset access ping #data-access and request the `redwood-datasets-read` role. Add your GitLab username for tracking. If you need S3 console access, open a ticket with the security team.

lauren: perfect, cloning dotfiles, adding npmrc, and will request dataset role. thanks everyone :raised_hands:

miguel: ping me if native builds still fail, happy to pair for the first install.
